title: A boy with messy black hair, bright green eyes, and a lightning-bolt scar, marked by an unsettling link to a dark enemy
clues: He learns on his eleventh birthday that he is famous in a hidden magical world he did not know existed.
He catches a tiny winged key in his first year, draws a sword from a Sorting Hat later on, and repeatedly survives encounters others would not.
A wand core twin to his enemy’s, a talent for flying, and the ability to speak to snakes set him apart even when he wishes they would not.
He becomes one of the few people to survive the Triwizard Tournament’s graveyard return and later walks willingly into the Forbidden Forest.
The piece of soul lodged in him explains why his scar burns and why he sometimes sees thoughts that are not his own.

title: A girl with bushy brown hair and large front teeth, carrying a relentless need to be prepared that even her friends sometimes underestimate
clues: Before her first train ride, she has already read nearly all her schoolbooks and begins correcting other students almost at once.
She brews Polyjuice Potion in a bathroom, solves Snape’s logic puzzle guarding the Stone, and traps a journalist in an unregistered beetle form.
Her handbag later carries almost impossibly many supplies because of an Undetectable Extension Charm.
She founds a society for house-elf rights and quietly wipes herself from her parents’ memories to protect them.
A Time-Turner once lets her attend overlapping classes long before she uses knowledge, law, and nerve in open resistance.

title: A lanky red-haired boy with a long nose and freckles, hiding deep insecurity beneath humor and unexpected nerve
clues: He grows up in a large wizarding family where hand-me-down robes, old pets, and secondhand wands are common facts of life.
His skill at wizard chess helps him win a life-sized match in first year, and he later imitates Parseltongue well enough to open a hidden chamber.
He is often overshadowed by brothers, famous friends, and his own self-doubt, which the locket Horcrux exploits mercilessly.
Though terrified of spiders after an early prank involving a teddy bear, he follows them into the Forbidden Forest anyway.
He leaves during the hunt but comes back to destroy the locket after pulling his best friend from an icy pool.

title: A tall wizard with a long silver beard and half-moon spectacles, concealing old guilt beneath wit, calm, and careful misdirection
clues: He is one of the very few wizards dark opponents openly feared, yet he often speaks in riddles and gentle observations rather than commands.
His office holds strange instruments, a phoenix, and a Pensieve through which crucial memories of the past are revealed.
He defeats Grindelwald in a legendary duel, discovers the twelve uses of dragon’s blood, and later drinks a terrible potion by a sea cave.
His left hand blackens after he puts on a ring that is more dangerous than it first appears.
He tells one boy that help will always be given at Hogwarts to those who ask for it, while privately planning far more than he says aloud.

title: A man with greasy black hair, a sallow face, and cold black eyes, driven by an old love he never stopped carrying
clues: Students know him for curt insults, sweeping black robes, and a classroom manner that can make brewing a potion feel like a duel.
He makes the counter-curse during a Quidditch match, teaches Occlumency badly, and writes old textbook spells under the name of a prince.
His bitterness toward one boy is sharpened by school memories of that boy’s father, yet his protection never entirely stops.
A silver doe leads someone to a sword hidden beneath ice, long after many readers have reason to mistrust him.
His final memories reveal that he asked only one thing in return for his service: to keep a green-eyed child alive for a woman with the same eyes.

title: A half-giant with beetle-black eyes and a tangled beard, unable to resist any creature that looks dangerous, rare, or misunderstood
clues: He arrives through storm and sea to tell a neglected boy the truth about his parents and his place in the magical world.
His hut is home to boars, hounds, dragons, and occasionally creatures that should plainly not be there.
He was expelled in his third year but still becomes the person many students trust first when fear or confusion sets in.
A broken pink umbrella hides more ability than most realize, and his giant blood later makes him unusually hard to stun.
He once wins a dragon egg from a hooded stranger by revealing exactly how to calm a three-headed dog.

title: A pale boy with pointed features and slick blond hair, masking fear with swagger learned from privilege and prejudice
clues: He reaches out early with the confidence of someone sure he knows who matters and who does not.
His insults toward Muggle-borns, his father’s influence, and his constant need to perform superiority make him a frequent school antagonist.
He joins the Inquisitorial Squad, becomes a Seeker, and later spends a year trying to repair a cabinet instead of mastering open violence.
A mission forced on him leaves him ill, frightened, and often alone in a bathroom where the pressure finally breaks him.
At a crucial moment atop a tower, he cannot bring himself to cast the final curse he was ordered to use.

title: A witch with square spectacles and a severe expression, combining tart discipline with a loyalty fiercer than many ever notice
clues: She is strict about rules, homework, and house points, yet her judgments are often sharper and kinder than students first think.
Her lessons begin by turning desks into pigs and continue through some of the most exacting magic taught at the school.
She once leaves a child on a doorstep after spending hours in cat form watching a perfectly ordinary street.
In battle she animates desks, suits of armor, and statues with a satisfaction rare for her usually controlled manner.
Under the tart comments and clipped tone is the Head of Gryffindor who quietly bends rules whenever courage deserves backing.

title: A tall figure with a snakelike face and red eyes, driven by a terror of death so extreme it twists every choice he makes
clues: Long before he loses his human features, he is a brilliant, charming student who steals trophies, asks dangerous questions, and collects followers.
He hides pieces of himself in a diary, a ring, a cup, a diadem, a locket, a snake, and something he never meant to use that way.
His rebirth in a graveyard uses bone, flesh, and blood, restoring a body that had existed for years only through possession and fragments.
He misunderstands sacrificial protection again and again because he values domination far above love.
A boyhood spent at an orphanage and a hatred of the father whose name he discards sit beneath the title he invents for himself.

title: A gaunt man with long dark hair and gray eyes, carrying reckless affection and old wounds behind a laugh that returns too quickly
clues: Once believed to have betrayed close friends, he escapes the prison no one is supposed to escape by using magic he was never officially registered to possess.
He is one of the Marauders and helps create a map that knows every corridor, passage, and moving resident of a castle.
A huge black dog begins appearing near a young hero long before the truth about this figure becomes clear.
His childhood home is full of dark objects, pure-blood prejudice, and a house-elf who despises him.
He offers a hunted boy a home more than once, even though he himself has never really had one.

title: A prematurely lined man in shabby robes, carrying quiet scholarship and deep self-disgust in equal measure
clues: He is one of the few teachers whose lessons students remember with uncomplicated gratitude, especially after boggarts, grindylows, and hinkypunks.
Chocolate is his first remedy after a soul-sucking encounter on a train, and practical kindness shapes much of his teaching.
He helped create a secret map as a schoolboy and once ran with friends who changed form to keep him company safely.
A forgotten potion and a full moon transform an admired professor into the danger he has always feared being.
He later tries to run from fatherhood before being forced to hear the truth about cowardice from someone much younger.

title: A round-faced boy with a poor memory and awkward manner, hiding stubborn heroism that grows strongest when adults fail him
clues: He is raised by relatives who measure him against a family legacy and once nearly discover his magic by dropping him from a window.
A lost toad and constant classroom mishaps make him seem comic early on, especially when potions are involved.
He improves dramatically in a resistance group, learns from a sympathetic Defence teacher, and later becomes one of a school’s fiercest defenders.
His parents still live, but not in any way that gives him back the childhood he should have had.
In the final battle he pulls a sword from a hat and destroys the last snake that matters.

title: A girl with straggly fair hair and protuberant eyes, wearing odd things with complete calm and seeing truth where others dismiss nonsense
clues: She reads upside down, says improbable things without embarrassment, and makes classmates uncomfortable only because she refuses their rules for normal.
People laugh at her beliefs about hidden creatures, yet she notices social cruelties and emotional realities that sharper minds miss.
She can see the skeletal winged carriage-pullers because she has already witnessed death.
She comments on wrackspurts, radishes, and dirigible-plum earrings with the same serene certainty she later brings to prison rescue and battle.
A painted ceiling in one friend’s room reveals how deeply treasured she feels the companionship others sometimes forget to offer her.

title: A small red-haired girl with bright brown eyes, possessing a fierce will that survives even after being used as someone else’s instrument
clues: At first she can barely speak in front of one famous boy, though that shyness disappears completely as she grows older.
A little black book becomes her confidant, then her captor, drawing her into acts she does not understand until far too late.
She later becomes a powerful flyer, a quick-casting duelist, and one of the sharpest wits in a crowded family.
Her Bat-Bogey Hex earns real respect, and her relationships never entirely overshadow her own force of character.
Long before the final war, she has already descended into a hidden chamber and lived.

title: A tall red-haired twin with a permanently amused face, turning danger into laughter even when the cost is rising around him
clues: He and his twin test sweets, invent joke goods, and treat rule-breaking as both an art and a public service.
A bewitched map, a flying car, and a spectacular swamp all benefit from his flair for chaos with purpose.
He leaves school in fireworks and dragon-shaped smoke, giving a headmistress one of the finest exits the castle has seen.
His jokes rarely mean he misses the truth; he notices fear, pomp, and hypocrisy quickly and answers each with mockery.
His final laugh comes in the middle of a war, moments before the twin bond at the center of so much mischief is broken forever.

title: A tall red-haired twin with identical features and a quicker undertone of tenderness, carrying grief no mirror can correct
clues: He builds inventions, sells portable chaos, and treats disruption as both defense and delight.
On one dangerous flight he loses part of himself to a curse aimed at something much worse.
Even after battle wounds, he keeps joking because humor is part of how his family survives fear.
He helps create a shop that turns schoolboy rebellion into a thriving business of tricks, disguises, and shield hats.
After the war, every laugh he makes has an absence beside it that no spell can restore.

title: A thin red-haired wizard with glasses and a distracted air, pairing gentle decency with an almost scholarly fascination for nonmagical objects
clues: He works in a Ministry office so small and unfashionable that ambition-seekers would never choose it willingly.
His delight in plugs, batteries, rubber ducks, and cars is sincere rather than mocking, which makes it all the more endearing.
He faces a giant snake in the line of duty and survives because someone far away sees through another’s eyes.
Though mild in manner, he can become unexpectedly sharp when pure-blood arrogance or cruelty toward the powerless surfaces.
He asks a question about the purpose of a rubber duck with exactly the seriousness others reserve for dragon law.

title: A plump red-haired witch with a warm face, hiding battle-grade ferocity beneath domestic fussing and knitted affection
clues: Her home is noisy, loving, patched together, and full of food, laundry, scolding, and the sort of safety children remember forever.
She sends sweaters, worries over lost sons, and can make a kitchen obey her wand while still spotting trouble across a crowded room.
A clock in her house tracks family members not by hour but by danger, work, travel, and mortal fear.
Her worst private fear emerges from a boggart that keeps reshaping itself into the bodies of those she loves.
In the final battle she proves that maternal tenderness and lethal magical skill can occupy the same wand hand.

title: A small house-elf with batlike ears and bulging green eyes, driven by a fierce hunger for freedom that makes him both troublesome and brave
clues: He first appears trying to save someone by ruining a dinner, sealing a gateway, and causing havoc no polite guest could ignore.
His language is self-punishing, his clothes are symbols, and his loyalty once given is more dangerous to enemies than they expect.
He masters Apparition in places where most wizards assume it should be impossible or forbidden.
A mismatched collection of hats, socks, and cast-off garments becomes a wardrobe of liberation rather than shame.
He dies on a beach after rescuing prisoners from a manor, and the grave is dug without magic.

title: A tall woman with heavy-lidded eyes and wild dark hair, turning devotion into cruelty with a joy that unsettles even allies
clues: She treats pain as performance, mockery as sport, and loyalty to her master as a kind of exalted calling.
A vault at Gringotts, a prison break from Azkaban, and a duel in the Department of Mysteries all bear her violent mark.
She tortures for information and for pleasure, leaving damage that does not end when the spell stops.
Her family connections tie her to old pure-blood lines, but she burns every ordinary bond for fanatic allegiance.
She kills a beloved fugitive cousin and later underestimates a mother who is no longer willing to retreat.

title: A pale aristocrat with long blond hair and a polished cane, disguising cowardice as refinement and influence as principle
clues: He moves easily through Ministry corridors, board politics, and drawing rooms where power wears expensive fabric.
A school governor’s vote, a cursed diary slipped into the wrong cauldron, and repeated denials all show how he prefers indirect harm.
His family name opens doors, yet the return of the master he once served reveals how little control privilege finally grants him.
He values blood purity and appearances, but terror begins to erode both once his household becomes a place of punishment.
The silver-headed cane vanishes from importance when fear replaces status at his own dinner table.

title: A pale woman with carefully arranged blond hair, letting family devotion outrank every ideology she once lived beside
clues: She belongs to an old pure-blood line and moves in the same circles that prize lineage, secrecy, and dark alliances.
Though not openly branded like some around her, she knows enough about fear and power to move carefully when both close in.
She makes a private vow for her son’s sake, even when that promise pulls her into perilous magic.
Her deepest loyalty is not to doctrine, status, or war, but to one boy she believes is being used.
A whispered lie in a forest changes the outcome of a battle because the answer she wants concerns only whether her child still lives.

title: A handsome, athletic boy with an easy manner, carrying a fairness that matters more than the applause surrounding him
clues: He is admired at school for talent and decency in nearly equal measure, which is rarer than the books let on at first.
He becomes a Triwizard champion and handles fame with less vanity than many older wizards would manage.
A clue about golden eggs, a prefects’ bathroom, and an underwater task all become part of his path.
He insists on honorable play even in Quidditch, asking for rematches where others would gladly keep a tainted win.
His death in a graveyard transforms a tournament tragedy into proof that the war has truly returned.

title: A pretty Ravenclaw with long dark hair, carrying visible composure over grief she cannot neatly control
clues: She is first noticed on a broomstick and later known through awkward conversations rather than dramatic speeches.
School romance, public pressure, and private mourning all entangle around her during one particularly difficult year.
Her connection to a champion lost in the tournament never entirely leaves the way others see her.
A date in a teashop becomes one of the most uncomfortable afternoons in the series because sorrow and jealousy are both present.
She joins a student resistance group even while carrying the complicated aftermath of bereavement and divided loyalties.

title: A squat woman with a toadlike face and a fondness for pink, masking bureaucratic sadism behind kitten plates and false sweetness
clues: She speaks in a simpering voice that makes cruelty sound like etiquette rather than punishment.
Educational decrees multiply around her until a school begins to feel less like a place of learning than a captured institution.
Detentions under her care leave words carved into skin without any visible blade.
She fears centaurs, loathes dissent, and mistakes petty authority for moral righteousness at every opportunity.
A blood quill, a sugar-coated cough, and a wall of decorative plates together create one of the series’ most hated presences.

title: A heavily scarred wizard with a magical blue eye, living by vigilance so absolute it has become both wisdom and wound
clues: He is famous as an Auror long before students meet him, mostly through stories of dark wizards caught and curses survived.
His trunk, his paranoia, and his booby-trapped habits all suggest a man who trusts preparation more than peace.
One school year linked to his name includes Unforgivable Curses in class, unusual helpfulness, and a cup touched at the wrong time.
The constant turning eye can see through wood, invisibility cloaks, and the backs of heads.
His motto becomes famous at school even though for much of that year the person saying it is not actually him.

title: A young witch with a frequently changing face and short, spiky hair, hiding deeper sadness beneath clumsiness and defiant humor
clues: She can alter her features at will, making disguise an instinct rather than a difficult spell.
Though often cheerful and physically awkward, she is a trained Auror trusted with dangerous work.
Her patronus changes after emotional upheaval, revealing feeling before she fully admits it aloud.
A disastrous war makes her seem dimmer for a time, not because her gift fades, but because hope does.
She rejects the first part of her own given name and marries a man who thinks he is too damaged to deserve her.

title: A tall bald wizard with a deep calm voice, concealing sharp strategic skill beneath effortless composure
clues: He serves within official structures while quietly helping resist the corruption spreading through them.
Even when other authorities flounder, he remains competent, discreet, and hard to unsettle.
He can direct protection for fugitives, deceive powerful colleagues, and still appear merely professional on the surface.
His patronus is among those used to send urgent warnings when collapse comes suddenly.
After the war, his steadiness proves so trusted that he helps lead the rebuilding of magical government.

title: A bald wizard with a large silver mustache, hiding shame behind genial appetite and a collector’s eye for promising people
clues: He likes comfort, candied fruit, velvet armchairs, and the reflected glow of famous former students.
His dinners and invitations form a private web of influence students jokingly name after him.
He avoids danger when he can, but not because he lacks talent; his preferred art is self-preservation.
One altered memory about a conversation with a gifted schoolboy becomes crucial to understanding a dark secret.
He returns to teach only after being coaxed out of hiding, where he has been disguising both his house and his conscience.

title: A short balding wizard with watery eyes and a ratlike face, burying opportunism beneath the appearance of weakness
clues: As a schoolboy he runs with brighter, braver friends whose loyalty he benefits from more than he deserves.
He becomes an unregistered Animagus not out of brilliance alone, but because fear can be patient and useful.
The wizarding world mourns him as a victim while the truth sits for years in a child’s pocket and sleeps in a cage.
He cuts off a finger, kills bystanders, and lets others carry the blame for betrayal on a massive scale.
A silver hand granted as reward later turns on him for a brief hesitation that suggests he once owed a life-debt.

title: A tall boy with untidy black hair and glasses, remembered for arrogance in youth but for loyalty and courage in the end
clues: He is popular, talented, and often infuriating at school, especially to one housemate who never forgets the humiliation.
With his closest friends he helps create a map that reveals secrets of a castle down to hidden passages and moving names.
He becomes an Animagus with antlers so that one friend will not face monthly suffering alone.
His worst memories involve swagger, teasing, and a dangerous confidence that takes years to outgrow.
He dies wandless in his own home after trying to hold off a killer long enough for his wife and child to run.

title: A young woman with dark red hair and bright green eyes, combining warmth, talent, and moral clarity stronger than fear
clues: She is born outside the magical world yet becomes one of the most gifted students of her year.
Her friendship with a lonely boy from a poor home shapes both his happiest memories and his worst future choices.
She eventually rejects cruelty and prejudice so completely that old affection cannot survive the difference.
A headmaster later describes her talent in charms and the brightness of her nature to someone who needs reminding.
Her refusal to step aside places ancient protection around her infant son and changes the entire course of the war.

title: A handsome wizard with gleaming blond curls and dazzling teeth, hiding cowardice behind polished vanity and stolen glory
clues: His books line shop windows and classroom lists, each one making him sound braver, cleverer, and busier than he really is.
He signs photographs of himself, smiles at danger, and assumes admiration is a substitute for competence.
Pixies, dueling clubs, and Valentine theatrics all go badly once actual skill is required instead of performance.
His specialty is not heroism but memory modification, which he uses to claim other people’s adventures as his own.
A broken wand reflects his final spell back on him, leaving him trapped in the kind of emptiness his fraud helped create.

title: A gaunt man with stringy hair and a sour expression, nursing private resentment because he lives in magic without sharing it
clues: He prowls corridors after curfew with a lantern, a cat, and an enthusiasm for punishment that students dread.
Chains, dungeons, and old disciplinary methods fascinate him in ways that reveal more than comic unpleasantness.
He knows the castle’s messes, stains, and rule-breakers intimately, even if students mostly notice only his bitterness.
A pamphlet about quick magical courses hints at a humiliation he would never willingly discuss in public.
His inability to perform spells makes every magical prank around him feel like mockery layered over exclusion.

title: A ghostly girl with thick glasses and a mournful voice, turning self-pity into unexpected usefulness for anyone patient enough to listen
clues: She haunts a bathroom, complains noisily, and measures insults with a memory that never seems to fade.
Students tend to avoid her until hidden passages, suspicious plumbing, and old school tragedies make her knowledge suddenly valuable.
She once followed a bully all the way home after death because grievance remained easier than peace.
A dangerous clue about eyes and sinks lies close to where she spends most of her afterlife.
She died when a monster opened its attack through a gaze she met near a set of taps.

title: A dark-haired young man with a hooked nose and heavy brows, combining world fame with an awkward reserve off the Quidditch pitch
clues: He arrives at school already known internationally, though his manner among classmates is far quieter than his reputation suggests.
On a broom he is angular, relentless, and capable of breathtaking dives that spectators remember instantly.
He enters the Triwizard Tournament and shows a colder, sterner magical seriousness than some of the other champions.
A library table conversation and a Yule Ball invitation reveal a shy side easy to miss beneath sporting celebrity.
Years later he is still prickly about symbols tied to dark magic, especially when he sees one hanging from another wizard’s neck.

title: A stunning young witch with silvery-blonde hair and an almost unearthly grace, concealing iron loyalty beneath elegance many mistake for vanity
clues: Her beauty affects people before she speaks, which often leads them to underestimate what firmness lies underneath.
She competes in the Triwizard Tournament and suffers setbacks that would reduce a less proud person to bitterness.
At first she can sound dismissive of rustic homes and school kitchens, yet affection changes how she speaks and what she values.
Her partial Veela heritage explains some of the reactions she inspires, but not the courage with which she faces war and injury.
When the face of the man she loves is ruined, she answers pity with outrage and proves she never wanted him only for looks.

title: A young man with a strained, restless look, burying fanatic intelligence beneath one of the longest deceptions in the series
clues: He vanishes from ordinary public life under scandal, secrecy, and a family arrangement rooted in fear and control.
A house-elf, a hidden room, and a father’s harsh ambition all play parts in how long his survival goes unnoticed.
For an entire school year, careful guidance and suspicious helpfulness push one student exactly where a dark master wants him.
Polyjuice Potion, a stolen magical eye, and a trunk with multiple compartments are essential to his masquerade.
His loyalty is so absolute that once revealed, he speaks with pride about delivering a boy to a graveyard rather than any remorse.

title: A stout wizard in a pinstriped cloak and bowler hat, preferring comfort and denial long after the facts turn dangerous
clues: He begins as a plausible authority figure, cordial enough in crisis so long as the crisis remains containable.
His fear of instability makes him distrust truth-tellers whenever the truth threatens his own position.
Newspapers, school inspections, and whisper campaigns become tools once simple persuasion no longer works.
He repeatedly mistakes bad news for political inconvenience instead of acting on evidence placed directly before him.
By the time he finally admits the return everyone else has risked their lives warning him about, the cost of delay is enormous.

title: A blonde witch with jeweled fingers and sharp glasses, turning gossip into weaponry by treating privacy as a problem to be overcome
clues: Her articles prefer scandal to fairness and implication to proof, especially when children can be made to look dramatic or unstable.
She knows details she should not know because she gathers them in ways both illegal and unannounced.
A tournament year gives her rich material: a famous boy, jealous classmates, grieving girls, and a school hungry for stories.
Even respected figures find themselves twisted into caricature once she gets ink and audience on her side.
Her unregistered beetle form finally traps her in a jar when someone more observant grows tired of being used.

title: A tall dark-haired Gryffindor with an easy manner, carrying quiet resilience through a history he understands only in pieces
clues: He is one of the steady background friends whose loyalty becomes more visible as the school years darken.
Posters, Quidditch talk, and dormitory life show him as sociable long before flight and hiding force a harder role.
He cannot prove a blood status that others suddenly decide matters, even though the truth about his family is more complicated than he knows.
On the run he travels with goblins, outcasts, and fellow fugitives before being captured and taken to a manor.
He was raised by Muggles because his wizard father died before revealing the truth to protect the family from dark enemies.

title: A sandy-haired boy with an expressive face, pairing loud humor with a talent for accidental explosions and eventual courage
clues: He begins as a lively Gryffindor whose magic has a habit of going off with more force than intended.
Dormitory scenes often place him amid jokes, sparks, and the kind of minor disaster that leaves soot behind.
For a time he believes official lies about a classmate more readily than friendship might excuse.
His mother’s caution shapes his views early, but war and experience push him toward a firmer understanding of where the danger lies.
By the final defense of the castle, he is blasting bridges and barricades instead of merely singeing feathers in class.

title: A tall red-haired wizard with horn-rimmed glasses and a pompous air, hiding loneliness beneath ambition and perfect posture
clues: He loves rules, titles, badges, and official approval with a sincerity his siblings find almost impossible not to mock.
As a student he patrols corridors, writes letters of reproof, and behaves as though school discipline is a sacred calling.
Ministry advancement tempts him into valuing career respectability over family trust when politics become toxic.
His estrangement lasts painfully long, especially for a household built on noisy closeness.
He returns at the battle with apologies, self-mockery, and more courage than his earlier choices had suggested.

title: A burly young wizard with a weathered Quidditch face, turning sporting determination into something close to military command
clues: He values practice schedules, tactical adjustments, and winning margins with an intensity that sometimes borders on mania.
New players are less recruited than conscripted once he decides they can help Gryffindor take the Cup.
Rain, broken brooms, rogue Bludgers, and even fainting spells rarely distract him from the larger campaign.
He can sound utterly tragic after a loss and utterly evangelical before a match, as though Quidditch contains the fate of kingdoms.
His captaincy is so consuming that even a deadly dog guarding a trapdoor briefly competes with match strategy for his attention.

title: An ancient house-elf with a shriveled body and muttering voice, concealing a bruised capacity for devotion beneath bitterness and prejudice
clues: He belongs to an old dark house and clings fiercely to its traditions, portraits, and grudges.
At first he seems only malicious, speaking insults under his breath and serving obedience poisoned by contempt.
A forgotten locket, a dead master’s impossible order, and an abandoned mission explain far more about him than his new owners know.
Kindness, proper authority, and the gift of a former master’s possessions transform him more effectively than punishment ever did.
When he leads elves into battle from the kitchens, the change is startling precisely because readers remember how nasty he once seemed.

title: A proud creature with steel-gray plumage and fierce orange eyes, ruled by ceremonial dignity that humans ignore at their peril
clues: He is neither horse nor bird, and any approach to him must begin with manners rather than ownership.
A first lesson in respect turns ugly when a student insults what he has not bothered to understand.
Chains, an appeal, and a pumpkin patch all become part of the effort to save him from a punishment born of political influence.
He later carries fugitives through dark skies and perches in caves as if exile were simply another landscape.
A bow offered properly earns his cooperation at once; disrespect earns claws faster than explanations can follow.

title: A translucent nobleman in a ruff, carrying old courtly pride and quiet embarrassment over a death that was almost, but not quite, complete
clues: He serves as a ghostly guide to one house of students, offering sympathy, gossip, and historical perspective in equal measure.
His longing for acceptance among the Headless Hunt reveals that even ghosts can remain painfully status-conscious.
Banquets for the dead, petrified students, and one locked cabinet all bring him into view at important moments.
His execution required many blows and still failed to separate head from neck cleanly enough to satisfy him centuries later.
He can hinge his head over one shoulder for effect, but never enough to win the club membership he wants.

title: A frail woman with enormous magnifying glasses and layers of shawls, performing vagueness so often that her rare real visions go almost unnoticed
clues: Most of her lessons involve tea leaves, mist, ominous sighs, and predictions of doom that could apply to nearly anyone.
Students often doubt her because theatricality surrounds almost everything she says and does.
Yet at key moments a stranger, harsher voice speaks through her, delivering truths others fail to understand in time.
Her job exists because of one prophecy overheard incompletely in a public house years before the school ever meets the boy concerned.
She is usually ridiculous until the books remind readers that two of the most consequential predictions in the series came from her mouth.

title: A squat witch with flyaway hair and earth-stained robes, combining practical warmth with an expert’s intimacy with dangerous plants
clues: She teaches in greenhouses where dirt, sap, pods, and roots matter more than polished wand flourishes.
Her students learn quickly that the magical world grows many things that heal, choke, sting, scream, or strangle depending on handling.
Though less dramatic than some teachers, she becomes crucial when a restorative plant is needed to reverse a schoolwide catastrophe.
Her house values loyalty and patience, qualities mirrored in the steady competence with which she runs lessons.
Mandrakes maturing under her care provide the cure that finally wakes victims petrified by a hidden monster.

title: A tiny wizard with a high voice and quick movements, pairing cheerful charm with formidable mastery too many students underestimate
clues: His classroom often rings with precise pronunciation, feather-lifting, and the sort of technical correction that seems gentle until one notices how exacting it is.
He conducts choirs, organizes enchanted decorations, and generally appears among the more approachable members of staff.
Yet in dueling and defensive magic he carries serious pedigree and no small amount of tactical value.
During the final battle he helps cast complex protective enchantments over the castle before joining the fight directly.
The same teacher who introduces students to Wingardium Leviosa is also a former dueling champion.
